1_wf_o1_cause: One classification mistake shared by intent but not by code: window spans live in OPENING_SPAN, so the second form (WALL_FACE x H - window rectangles + lintels + heads) loses the wall plane through every window and then also deducts the window rectangle; windows have no below-sill / above-head surfaces at all in V1.
2_v2_fix: One wall-plane identity: every span on a wall line (wall face, window, door, sliding door, floor-reaching glazing) belongs to the plane; an opening removes exactly its rectangle clipped to [0, H]. METHOD A from the conservation pass: (sum of plane span lengths) x H - sum of rectangles + head faces. METHOD B from explicitly generated surface records: WALL_FACE (full-height spans) + BELOW_SILL (w x sill) + ABOVE_OPENING (w x (H - top)) + HEAD_FACE. Different data paths, predeclared tolerance, any mismatch -> BLOCKED; a separate reconcile() is tested against a deliberately broken surface list; every area test asserts state == COMPUTED.

No Urban constant.

Floor-to-floor alone is never a wall height.

9_reveal_authority_separation: Physical reveal (geometry + owning side, from frame / leaf / track position) is kept apart from its FINISH state: PLASTER_DEFAULT (owner rule), PLASTER_AND_PAINT (only when the owning side is a painted dry surface), PORCELAIN_EXPLICIT (only with explicit authority), OTHER_EXPLICIT, UNRESOLVED (ownership or surface not established - that reveal only). A wet / service owner never gets paint by default.
10_profile_position: The frame / track plane splits the wall depth: each side owns the depth between its face and the nearest frame line; a frame flush with a face leaves that side no reveal. A reveal face not drawn on its side (cavity) is UNRESOLVED, never invented.
